state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you explain why you think the range wouldn't change if all the plants were cut in half or grew by \(3 \mathrm{~cm}\) each? What do you think the range represents in this situation?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I think the range is like the difference between the biggest and smallest plant, so it would be 42 minus 13 which is 29 cm. But I'm confused because if we cut all the plants in half, wouldn't the biggest and smallest also get smaller, so the difference between them would still be the same? I'm not really sure why Katie would be wrong though...

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of a situation where changing all values by the same proportion would actually change the range? Consider how the relationship between the largest and smallest values might be affected in that scenario.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Hmm, so like... if we add 3 cm to each plant, the biggest is still 3 cm bigger than it was before, and the smallest is also 3 cm bigger, so the difference stays 29 cm, right? But when we cut them in half, like 42 divided by 2 is 21 and 13 divided by 2 is 6.5, so that's still a difference of 14.5... oh wait, that's not 29 anymore! So Tom is actually wrong too?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the proportional change misconception through well-calibrated questioning that leads the student to discover independently that halving changes the range while adding a constant does not, demonstrating clear conceptual progress from initial confusion to correct understanding.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking, never provides direct answers, and allows the student to discover their own misconception about proportional changes through guided inquiry.
